Apple'𝐬 𝐀𝐈 𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐠𝐲 𝐢𝐬𝐧'𝐭 𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐪𝐮𝐞, 𝐢𝐭'𝐬 𝐚 𝐠𝐚𝐦𝐞-𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐫.

𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐫𝐞𝐞-𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐚𝐜𝐡 𝐭𝐨 𝐀𝐈 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐝𝐬 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐢𝐳𝐞𝐬 𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐜𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐟𝐮𝐧𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲.

𝐖𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐛𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐭?

Apple's AI strategy is about:
1. On-device computations
2. Private cloud compute
3. Third-party inferences.

This vertical integration lets Apple control costs, privacy, and hardware markets.

On-device AI processes small, low-latency tasks.

Private cloud is for complex tasks secured via encrypted transmissions.

Third-party models, like ChatGPT, enables them to collect high quality data from the leading models resulting in continuous improvement of their own models.

This integrated approach accelerates device upgrades and enhances user experiences. 

It also positions Apple's models to become close to GPT-4o level.

As product managers, think what could be your version of vertical integration to capitalize on with your AI strategy.

As 2024 unfolds, the buzz around ChatGPT Enterprise's growth is loud, yet DNS records quietly tell the true story of its early adopters. 

DNS records, which verify a company’s domain during ChatGPT Enterprise subscription, show us which companies truly invest in this technology as analyzed by Henley Wing Chiu.

1️⃣ Only 5% of Fortune 500 companies use ChatGPT Enterprise. This low adoption rate signals a significant potential for growth within top-tier companies.

2️⃣ Major companies maintaining bans on ChatGPT haven't reversed their decisions. Despite the hype, companies like JP Morgan Chase, Apple, Amazon, and Spotify continue to restrict use due to security and data privacy concerns.

3️⃣ Tech and finance sectors lead in ChatGPT adoption. Their drive for competitive advantage makes them more open to innovative AI solutions.

4️⃣ ChatGPT Enterprise companies are not accelerating AI talent hiring. This suggests a balanced approach to AI integration, rather than a rush for expertise.

These insights offer AI product managers a clearer view of the enterprise AI landscape and strategic positioning for effectively deploying AI solutions in a competitive market.

text:
90 days ago, I started a new journey as an AI product leader, equipped with insights from seasoned product leaders. 

I focused on 4 foundational steps that seemed to be overlooked by many.

1️⃣ 𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩𝐬

Connecting with my colleagues was my first priority.
I arranged one-on-one meetings to learn more about their experiences and perspectives.
These conversations focused on them, fostering genuine connections.
It’s easy to dive into operational work conversations but try to refrain from that at first. 

2️⃣ 𝐃𝐞𝐞𝐩 𝐄𝐧𝐠𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐎𝐮𝐫 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐬

I immersed myself in using our suite of products and speaking with customers.
Regular discussions with peers helped clarify the intent behind each product choice.
As an AI leader, it’s key to understand how the product/s works and the customers' perspectives.

3️⃣ 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐧𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐓𝐨𝐩 𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐬

I also sought insights from the company's top performers.
By asking who others admired, I compiled a list of influential figures and arranged meetings to learn from their experiences.
I looked for common patterns, made a log of their documents and read them thoroughly to learn how they strategize within the company.

4️⃣ 𝐖𝐞𝐞𝐤𝐥𝐲 𝐔𝐩𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬

To keep track of my progress, I wrote weekly updates to my manager.
Named 'State of Udi', these reports detailed my key activities, challenges, thoughts and priorities for the following week, helping me maintain clarity and communicate effectively with my manager.

The intentional approach to these first 90 days was about laying a solid foundation for success, ensuring my efforts aligned closely with both team dynamics and company goals.

These steps, often overlooked, are essential for integrating and making a marked impact in a new role.

Understanding these Generative AI trends could be the difference between leading and lagging in 2024.

𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐭𝐨𝐩 𝟓 𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐬:

𝟏. 𝐄𝐦𝐩𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐢𝐬 𝐨𝐧 𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐯𝐬. 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐆𝐞𝐧𝐀𝐈 

In 2024, creating custom GenAI solutions is the focus. 

Enterprises are preferring to build their GenAI tech rather than buying off-the-shelf products. 

This means AI product managers must focus more on developing customizable, flexible GenAI platforms. 

𝟐. 𝐈𝐧𝐜𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐈𝐧𝐯𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐢𝐧 𝐆𝐞𝐧𝐀𝐈 𝐓𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐭 

The demand for AI talent is skyrocketing. 

AI product managers must focus on attracting and nurturing specialized AI skills within their teams. 

For instance, a product manager might prioritize hiring data scientists proficient in language model fine-tuning. 

As teams grow, they will also need AI product managers to guide the strategy,  make sure they are focused on the right things and communicate well across the company.

𝟑. 𝐒𝐡𝐢𝐟𝐭 𝐓𝐨𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐝𝐬 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐧 𝐒𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐜𝐞 𝐌𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐬 

Open source is the new frontier in GenAI. 

Open-source models offer flexibility and community support, which is vital for innovation. 

Product managers need to embrace open-source AI models for greater agility and innovation.

𝟒. 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐈𝐦𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐄𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐆𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 

Ethical AI is becoming non-negotiable. 

Product managers must integrate ethical considerations into their AI products from the start. 

An example might be implementing bias checks in LLMs. 

Ensuring GenAI products are ethical and responsible is crucial for trust and sustainability.

𝟓. 𝐂𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐢𝐳𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐂𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐌𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐬 

Tailored solutions take center stage. 

Product managers should focus on customizing existing language models to fit specific needs. 

A practical approach could involve fine-tuning a general language model for niche applications. 

Customization ensures products are relevant and efficient.

𝐌𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐚𝐝𝐚𝐩𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐝𝐨𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐝𝐨𝐰𝐧 𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐞 𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐥𝐚𝐠 𝐢𝐧 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟒.

The future of Generative AI is being written in the code of today's open source projects.

A recent analysis by Chip Huyen on the 900 most popular open source Generative AI related Github repos reveal the key trends product managers should be aware of.

1️⃣ 𝐀𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐔𝐬𝐞𝐫-𝐅𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐫

Applications are where AI directly meets user needs.

The most popular types are coding tools, interactive bots such as those used in WhatsApp and Slack, and applications for information aggregation.

This shows a clear preference for AI that aids in productivity and communication.

2️⃣ 𝐀𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐃𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐩𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭: 𝐁𝐫𝐢𝐝𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐌𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐔𝐬𝐞𝐫𝐬

Application development now goes beyond basics.

It includes advanced prompt engineering, diverse AI interfaces like web apps and chatbots, and comprehensive frameworks for building and evaluating AI applications.

This evolution points to AI becoming more user-friendly and integrated into daily tools.

3️⃣ 𝐌𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥 𝐃𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐩𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐧𝐨𝐯𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

Model development has shifted significantly.

It's now heavily focused on refining models for efficiency and accuracy. Inference optimization has leaped from 16-bit to 2-bit quantization, a major efficiency boost.

Evaluation methods, including innovative approaches like AI-as-a-judge, are enhancing model reliability.

This layer's evolution signals a robust commitment to developing more effective and accountable AI models.

4️⃣  𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐫𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐋𝐚𝐲𝐞𝐫

The infrastructure layer is all about supporting AI operations.

Notably, the introduction of vector databases like Qdrant and Pinecone signals a shift towards more sophisticated data handling in AI.

Use these open source insights to guide your Generative AI strategies, staying ahead in a rapidly evolving AI landscape.

A focus on a single critical decision can offer a window into their problem-solving approach.

3. 𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐚𝐜𝐡 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐭, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐰𝐡𝐲?  
This prompts reflection on choices and the reasoning behind them.

4. 𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐦𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐝𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐝𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐈 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭? 
Surprises often lead to the most valuable insights.

5. 𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐥𝐞 𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐩𝐥𝐞 𝐡𝐚𝐬 𝐛𝐞𝐞𝐧 𝐦𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐢𝐧 𝐠𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐀𝐈 𝐝𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐩𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭? 
This distills their experience into a fundamental takeaway.

These questions are designed to drive thoughtful responses that provide deep insights while remaining straightforward and engaging.

The moment a product manager truly understands a data scientist, AI innovation takes a giant leap forward. 

I know this first hand as I led AI & data teams for the past decade and constantly bridged the gaps with product managers.

Here are the 5 key takeaways for product managers to communicate better with data scientists:

𝟏. 𝐁𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐈𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐭
Align AI projects with business outcomes, not just technical achievements. Show data scientists their work's direct ROI impact. 
Avoid technical jargon; focus on business value.

Alignment with business impact guides effective AI development.


𝟐. 𝐂𝐥𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐢𝐧 𝐎𝐛𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐬
Clear goals align teams. 
Say, "Improve model accuracy to 90%," not "Use X algorithm." 
Specific, clear objectives guide data scientists without limiting their approach.

Clarity in goals ensures targeted outcomes.

𝟑. 𝐈𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐞𝐬𝐬
Plan for iterative, adaptable development. 
Involve data scientists in scenario planning. 
This flexible approach respects AI's experimental nature.

Iterative planning embraces AI's unpredictability.

𝟒. 𝐑𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐯𝐞 𝐁𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐫𝐬
Find out what’s in the data scientists' way and help clear it. 
AI related roadblocks such as data or infra resources can delay work significantly.

Support from product managers can expedite problem-solving.

𝟓. 𝐑𝐞𝐠𝐮𝐥𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧
Keep all informed on AI project phases and changes. 
Avoid technical ambiguity; clarity builds trust. 

Regular updates unite teams towards common goals.

Effective communication with data scientists combines empathy, clarity, and support, leading to successful AI innovations.

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐭𝐨 𝐔𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐂𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐖𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐁𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐘𝐨𝐮 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐭

Many AI projects fail because they don't really know what the customer needs. 

It's a common mistake. Your AI is smart, but is it useful?

As AI product leaders, we're also selling solutions. 

Thanks to insights from Chris Orlob, who grew Gong to $200M ARR, I learned and tested the art of asking the right questions👇

1️⃣ "𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭'𝐬 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐛𝐢𝐠𝐠𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐠𝐞 𝐰𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐢𝐭 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐗?"
• It's the opener. It gets to the heart of their issue.
• It starts the dialogue on what really matters. 

2️⃣ "𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭'𝐬 𝐠𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧 𝐢𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐛𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭'𝐬 𝐝𝐫𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐛𝐞 𝐚 𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐨𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐲?"
• This uncovers the deeper 'why.'
• It connects the challenge to their current business climate. 

3️⃣ "𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐦𝐞𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐜 𝐢𝐬 𝐬𝐮𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐦𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐚𝐬 𝐚 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐮𝐥𝐭 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭?"
• This identifies the pain in numbers.
• It's all about the tangible impact on their operations. 

4️⃣ "𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭'𝐬 𝐝𝐫𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐭𝐨 𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐯𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐰 𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫?"
• This question reveals urgency.
• It shows the immediate need and potential for quick wins. 

Getting deep into these will help you focus your AI product or feature on real needs. 

These aren't just questions; they're tools to align your AI's value with the customer's crisis points.

text:
The LNO Framework by @shreyas Doshi: A Proven 3-Step Strategy for Product Managers to Achieve Peak Efficiency and Balance 

Most productivity methods fail, but the LNO Framework is different.

1. L Tasks (Leverage) 

Leverage tasks are crucial. They demand your best energy.

L tasks drive key outcomes. Tackle these in your peak hours. An example: writing your product strategy. This ensures your vital tasks receive the focus they need.

Prioritize L tasks for impact.

2. N Tasks (Neutral) 

Neutral tasks are essential but less impactful.

N tasks support your daily workflow. They don't require your highest energy but are necessary. Routine meetings are N tasks. These tasks maintain project momentum.

Balance with N tasks.

3. O Tasks (Overhead) 

Overhead tasks are low priority but necessary.

O tasks require minimal energy. Handle these when multitasking. Examples include clearing emails or administrative work. Use AI for these tasks to free up more time for L and N tasks.

Manage O tasks quickly.

Embracing the LNO Framework changes how you prioritize as a product manager. 

The real twist? 

Generative AI can help with many of your N and O tasks, allowing you to devote more energy to high-impact L tasks.

While AI continues to evolve rapidly, the constants of product management are found in Shreyas Doshi's time-tested frameworks.

With over 15 years of experience at top tech companies, Shreyas is the ultimate PM mentor.

His insights, more relevant than ever in the fast-paced AI domain, are crucial for product managers 👇 

1️⃣ 𝐏𝐫𝐞 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐦𝐬: 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐀𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐀𝐈

AI projects are unpredictable.

Most do Post Mortems, but Pre Mortems help you prepare.

AI Product Management can be hectic.

Expectations for magic are high, and you have a lot on your plate.
The LNO Framework sorts tasks into Leverage, Neutral, and Overhead. 
High-energy times are for strategic tasks where you want to spend your best time.

This method ensures you're focusing your best efforts where they'll have the most effect in AI.

3️⃣ 𝐓𝐡𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐋𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐥𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐤 - 𝐄𝐈𝐎: 𝐀 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐭𝐞 𝐕𝐢𝐞𝐰

AI isn't just about building.

It's about the big picture.
Balancing Execution, Impact, and Optics is key.
This means not just doing the work, but understanding its wider impact and how it's seen.

Balancing these three areas is crucial to being a good AI PM.

In AI, the future can be more important than immediate returns, and you can easily spend weeks not moving the needle.

Focusing on opportunity costs helps AI PMs make decisions for long-term success.

It's about choosing paths with the greatest future potential, not just quick wins.

5️⃣ 𝐇𝐢𝐠𝐡 𝐀𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐲: 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐲𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐀𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐀𝐈

Adaptability is key in AI's fast-paced world.

High Agency means being proactive and flexible, essential in AI product management.

It's about leading change, not just following it, in a constantly evolving field.

text:
𝐀 𝐒𝐢𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐲 𝐓𝐨 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐤 𝐀𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐋𝐋𝐌 𝐄𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐮𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭 𝐌𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐫𝐬

There was a time when LLM evaluation was a daunting task, but that's changing rapidly. 

Let's break it down into simpler terms for a clearer understanding.
Imagine LLMs as a smart conversation partner. 
To evaluate how good it is, we mainly use two methods 👇 

𝟏. 𝐔𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐋𝐋𝐌'𝐬 𝐎𝐮𝐭𝐩𝐮𝐭:
Think of an LLM like a game of predicting the next word in a sentence.

We check if the LLM guesses the next word (or group of words) correctly.
It's like giving the LLM a partial sentence and seeing how well it completes it.

We compare the LLM's guesses with what we expected to see if it's on the right track.

𝟐. 𝐂𝐡𝐞𝐜𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐋𝐋𝐌'𝐬 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲𝐭𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐒𝐤𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐬:
Here, the LLM is like a storyteller.

We let the LLM create a whole piece of text, like a short story.
Then, we introduce a unique twist: we turn LLMs into a judge.
Not only does it generate text, but it also evaluates its own narrative, just as a seasoned editor scrutinizes a draft.

We compare this self-assessment with expert evaluations to ensure the story is logical and engaging.

𝐓𝐡𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐠𝐡 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐦𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥, 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭 𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐚𝐥𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐋𝐋𝐌 𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐮𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧.

text:
𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐮𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐀𝐈 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐒𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐫, 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐳𝐞𝐝 𝐋𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐮𝐚𝐠𝐞 𝐌𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐬

Meta and Microsoft's new GPUs might just be the building blocks for an AI that's not about size, but about smarts.

𝟏.  𝐇𝐮𝐠𝐞 𝐀𝐈 𝐦𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐬 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐬.

Large models have their advantages, but there's a turning point where scale no longer equates to better performance. Compact models like Phi-2 are emerging, providing efficiency and specialized expertise.

Small models adapt quicker to niche needs.

𝟐. 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐧-𝐬𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐜𝐞 𝐀𝐈 𝐢𝐬 𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐦𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐬.

The shift towards open-source AI is creating a collaborative environment. This approach allows for a diverse range of inputs, potentially leading to AI models that rival proprietary giants.

Open-source AI promotes diverse innovation.

𝟑. 𝐒𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐠𝐢𝐜 𝐟𝐨𝐜𝐮𝐬 𝐨𝐧 𝐜𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐢𝐳𝐞𝐝 𝐬𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐫 𝐦𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐬 𝐲𝐢𝐞𝐥𝐝𝐬 𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐟𝐮𝐧𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐛𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐟𝐢𝐭𝐬.

Focusing on smaller models allows organizations to develop AI that is both budget-friendly and purpose-built. For example, Microsoft's Orca2 demonstrates the feasibility of creating task-specific AI without incurring significant costs.

Targeted AI solutions enhance value and efficiency.

It seems so, according to recent research.

These research-backed prompting techniques can transform your LLM interactions:

𝟏. 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐭 𝐒𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐂𝐥𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐲
Begin with a precise structure.
This sets the stage for effective communication.

Example: “###Instruction### Explain [specific topic] in simple terms.”

𝟐. 𝐒𝐩𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐟𝐢𝐜𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧
Be specific and request unbiased information.

Example: “Ensure your answer is unbiased and does not rely on stereotypes.”

Why it works: It leads to more accurate and impartial LLM responses.

𝟑. 𝐔𝐬𝐞𝐫 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐄𝐧𝐠𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭
Create a dialogue.
Encourage the LLM to ask questions for better understanding.

Example: “I would like you to ask me questions to gather more information.”

Why it works: It turns one-way commands into a dynamic conversation, enhancing clarity.

𝟒. 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐋𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐮𝐚𝐠𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐲𝐥𝐞
Direct and straightforward language is key.
Politeness should be left out.

Example: Drop phrases like “please” and “thank you.”

Why it works: Eliminates unnecessary language, leading to more direct and efficient LLM responses.

𝟓. 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐱 𝐓𝐚𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐭𝐬
For complex tasks, use a step-by-step approach.

Example: “Break this task into smaller steps. Start with [first step].”

Why it works: Simplifies complex tasks, making them more manageable for the LLM.

The research shows that clear, structured, and specific prompts can significantly improve LLM performance across many models tested.

In generative AI, the balance between speed and quality is crucial. Product managers face tough choices.

1. What Are the User Expectations and Needs?

Understanding user expectations is key in AI development.

For news AI, fast updates matter. Users want quick info.

In investment research, however, depth and accuracy are crucial.

Your AI's focus must align with user demands.

2. What is the Risk of Inaccuracy?

Error potential is a critical consideration.

For a travel recommendation AI, minor inaccuracies might be acceptable. But in financial recommendations AI, even small errors can lead to significant problems.

Minimize risks by prioritizing accuracy.

3. What is the Cost Implication?

Cost considerations influence AI model choice.

A specialized model may have higher initial costs but offer long-term savings and control. Conversely, general models might be quicker to deploy but can incur higher ongoing costs and offer less customization.

Balance initial costs with long-term value and control.

Consider your strategy carefully. Balancing speed versus quality in AI will be your biggest trade off and define your AI product's success.

4 Levels of Specializing Large Language Models (LLMs) for AI Products

Choosing the right way to specialize your LLM is crucial for a product’s success. Each level offers unique solutions for different needs.

1. Prompt Engineering with Context

Need simple tasks? Start here.

Define the task’s scope, and you can get basic but crucial tasks done efficiently.

For example, an LLM can create focused marketing content if you guide it correctly.

It's about smartly directing LLMs to meet your goals.

2. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)

Need access to external data or documents to enhance output quality?  

Use RAG. It lets the LLM fetch and use external data, enriching its responses.  

For example, an AI assistant that can answer questions from your product documentation.

This approach enhances the LLM's output with added information.

3. Fine-Tuned Model

Need specific expertise?

Fine-tune your LLM with targeted data for accuracy in a particular field.

SQLCoder-34B by Defog.ai (YC W23) is a great example, specialized in translating natural language into SQL queries.

Fine-tuning ensures your LLM delivers precision in its specialty.

4. Trained Model

Does your product have unique needs?

If standard LLMs can’t meet these, consider creating a model from scratch. This is essential for complex, specialized tasks.

JPMorgan's DocLLM is a prime example, crafted to process complex financial documents, showcasing the power of a custom LLM.

Custom-trained models solves for more unique and complex demands.

text:
Where is data going with generative technology? 

The recent Data Council conference in Austin showcased some of the most exciting trends and innovations in the industry, including the proliferation of AI tooling and the simplification of development processes. With these advancements, data teams and businesses have the potential to become truly data-driven and revolutionize their industries.

Here are some of the key takeaways:
The Activity Schema simplifies answering questions using SQL for event-driven analytics.
Streaming and real-time data solutions are being redefined by tools like Bytewax and Materialize, making them more accessible to teams.
There is a major focus on lineage, governance, and observability, with Datahub and Datafold being promising solutions.
Snowflake and BigQuery are becoming the standard for DWH solutions, with Redshift falling out of favor.
AI tooling is proliferating, and there's a shift towards simplification of development processes.
Faster frameworks like Rust, Arrow, and Duckdb are gaining traction in the data community.
DBT is still the go-to for data transformation, and Fivetran is the industry standard for data ingestion.
Hex is emerging as a great platform for ad-hoc analysis, and Dagster is a more developer-friendly alternative to Airflow.

With so many exciting advancements and trends in the world of data, it's an exciting time to be part of a data team or business looking to become truly data-driven. Stay tuned for my upcoming posts on how to leverage generative AI within data teams to take advantage of these trends and revolutionize your industry.

#datastrategy #generativeai

text:
We've all heard of the last mile in ecommerce, but now it's time to pay attention to the last mile of AI. 
Businesses are trying to leverage generative AI for everything, but the leap from 80% to 100% accuracy takes work. In fact, it can take much longer than the jump to 80%. This presents new business opportunities for those who can nail the last mile of generative AI. So, how can you do it? Here are three key elements to focus on:

Domain specific processing of data: Your algorithms are as good as the feature inputs, you need to focus on domain-specific pre and post-processing of the data that enters and exits the language models.

Unique data access: You need access to unique data sets to create a network effect within your product.

Deep domain expertise: Understanding the 80% to 100% jump is crucial to creating an impactful experience for your end users. 80% isn't enough for most business use cases. Ensure you have deep domain expertise to achieve this.

By mastering these three elements, you can excel in the last mile of generative AI and leverage new business opportunities. 
#AI #data #AIlastmile #generativeAI

text:
ScaleUp:AI NYC was one of the top AI/ML conferences ever organized and I was excited to be invited in person. Insight Partners did a great job gathering the top AI/ML leaders of the world.

Here are my 3 biggest takeaways reflecting on last week:

1. AI evolution is just at the beginning but it will be a lot faster than the software evolution. Companies who set themselves up with optimal data infrastructure, invest heavily in AI/ML, and hire top talent early on will thrive and win big.

2. The world is moving to a more data-centric versus model-centric view of AI, where good data is more important than big data. Spend most of the time systematically engineering data to be high quality, complete and reliable. It’s the key to succeed with AI use cases at scale.

3. Combine machine intelligence with human intelligence and integrate layers of AI from different paradigms. Combined AI benefits from the best of both worlds. Example: Merge time series prediction with NLP based on features engineered together with subject matter experts.

Join our AI scale-up journey at OpenWeb, we are hiring for many roles in the data team (details in the first comment or DM me).
